trigger: Twelve firm URLs fed to a single collector built against RSM; eleven returned nothing.
diagnosis: Asked heal to rewrite the extraction to cover eleven unseen layouts generically.
resolution: heal ran for 40 minutes through code_fixer and returned status: error. Scraper Studio generates extraction code against a specific site and heal repairs a collector against its own target; it will not port one to unrelated domains. The collector was left untouched, which is how we learned heal is non-destructive. Architecture changed to one collector per layout.

trigger: Markup changed deliberately: CSS classes renamed and the headline nested one level deeper.
diagnosis: The page layout changed and the scraper returned no articles at all. The class names and element nesting it matched on no longer exist.
resolution: Repaired unattended. Same collector ID, nothing downstream touched.

trigger: Contract reported published_date at 47%. Investigated after heal returned done with nothing altered.
diagnosis: The scraper was not broken. BDO's listing mixes dated articles with evergreen podcast hubs, an eBook summary and an assessment tool, none of which carry a publication date. The contract had assumed every listed item is dated.
resolution: Contract corrected, not the scraper: partial date coverage is content, below 25% is a break. This is why the loop re-runs and re-validates rather than trusting a done status.

trigger: Found by the contract on a routine run. Not staged.
diagnosis: 'article_url' was empty on 20 of 20 articles and 'published_date' on 20 of 20. Both selectors had stopped matching the article cards.
resolution: Repaired across two code_fixer rounds inside one heal, auto-approved and saved.

trigger: Seven of thirteen sources reported 'Crawler error: Navigation failed ... too many'.
diagnosis: Read as broken selectors, the contract named five healthy firms in a heal prompt.
resolution: Not a scraper problem: three orphaned fleet runs were racing each other, so Marcum was being scraped by four concurrent jobs. Running a collector is rate limited at the crawler, separately from the AI-Flow generation cap. Concurrency reduced to 2, and the contract taught to separate a failed run from a break so heal is never dispatched at one.

trigger: scraper create returned poll_failed: 'Timeout after 600 seconds waiting for AI generation'.
resolution: Generation had completed server-side after the CLI stopped watching. The collector returns 20 clean rows and was nearly discarded. A client-side poll timeout is not evidence a collector is dead: run it before rebuilding.

trigger: Never returned a row, including with zero competing runs.
diagnosis: The run times out after ten minutes rather than returning an error envelope.
resolution: Open. Not a contention victim and not a selector break the contract can describe; reported honestly as a source that has never worked rather than counted as coverage.

trigger: Never returned a row, including with zero competing runs.
diagnosis: The run exits non-zero and writes no output.
resolution: Open. Same treatment as Marcum: counted as a source that has never worked.
